primary_claim: Instruction tuning compresses attention-entropy-based self-referent processing toward neutral fact-retrieval processing in English-centric models (Llama, Mistral), while a multilingual model (Qwen) largely preserves the distinct attention pattern between self-referent and neutral prompts after instruction tuning.

effect.metric: mean change in Role-Focus Coefficient (ΔRFC) from base to instruct, by model
effect.value: Llama 3.1 8B: -0.023 (68.8% of layers compress); Mistral 7B: -0.093 (81.2% compress); Qwen 2.5 7B: +0.048 (28.6% compress, 50% near zero)

stated_future_work: Test the linguistic hypothesis by comparing Qwen's behavior on Chinese versus English self-referent prompts
Run token-position-controlled prompt experiments to identify if specific tokens drive the observed attention patterns
Extend the RFC framework to other safety-relevant questions, such as goal-directed or planning behaviours
Attempt activation patching by transplanting English-centric base model head activations into instruct models
Apply SAEs to decompose what features candidate heads are computing
limitations_stated: Attention entropy at the layer level is a noisy statistic, and it will be difficult to identify if there's a real circuit to examine
Sample sizes are small (30 prompts for Mistral/Llama, only 20 for Qwen due to crashing issues)
The 'confounder' prompt category might be misnamed, conflating implied second-person and first-person pronoun effects
All evidence presented is purely suggestive
quote: English-centric models (Mistral, Llama) show compression of layer-wise self-referent processing attention patterns toward neutral fact-retrieval patterns, while a multilingual model (Qwen) preserves the distinct attention patterns
